title: The Enterprise View
briefing: As Head of Risk you own the enterprise risk profile. The executive sees 140 operational risks and no picture of what could actually stop Valtren meeting its strategy.
Build the enterprise view: the handful of risks that matter at board level.

context.text: Because every unit now uses one method, you can aggregate their registers for the first time.
Losing Pellmoor's pharma client has hit the strategic plan; the board wants to know what else could.

evidence.title: Strategic objectives
evidence.body: 1. Pharma to 25% of revenue in three years. 2. Margin from 7% to 9%. 3. Net-zero fleet by 2035. 4. Keep top-3 client retention.

evidence.title: Aggregated unit risks (examples)
evidence.body: Six sites each list 'compressor failure'. Four list 'driver shortage'. Three list cyber outage of route planning. Two list refrigerant regulation.

evidence.title: External scan
evidence.body: Refrigerant phase-down regulation tightening in 2027; electric refrigerated trucks two years from viable range; pharma clients consolidating suppliers.

questions.prompt: What does an enterprise risk look like compared with a unit risk?

options.label: It threatens a strategic objective and often aggregates unit risks, e.g. cold-chain failure built from compressor, logger and fleet risks
It is the highest-scoring risk in any unit's register, escalated because of its size
options.feedback: Size alone misses aggregation and strategic relevance.

options.label: It is a risk that appears in every business unit's register, so it is company-wide by definition and needs an executive owner
options.feedback: Frequency is a clue, not a definition.

questions.prompt: Which belong on the enterprise profile?

options.label: Cold-chain integrity failure loses pharma accreditation or a key client
Driver and engineer shortage constrains growth and safety
Refrigerant and fleet transition outpaces Valtren's plan

questions.prompt: How do you present the profile to the executive?

options.label: One page: 8-10 enterprise risks, each with owner, trend, appetite status, link to objectives and key actions
options.feedback: A view an executive can use in one meeting.

options.label: All 140 risks ranked by residual score, with filters by unit, so nothing important is lost in the aggregation
options.feedback: The problem the profile was meant to solve.

options.label: A heat map of the 140 risks on one page, colour-coded by business unit
options.feedback: Shows position but not owners, trend or actions.

questions.prompt: Who should own the enterprise risks?

options.label: Individual executives, each accountable for one or two, reporting to the board risk committee
options.feedback: Enterprise risks need owners with enterprise authority.

options.label: The risk team, which can see across units and has no conflict of interest
options.feedback: The second line oversees; it doesn't own business risks.

options.label: The unit heads who reported the underlying risks, since they manage the controls day to day
options.feedback: They own the parts, not the aggregate.

questions.prompt: The refrigerant regulation is three years out. Include it now?

options.label: Yes: fleet and plant decisions made now decide whether Valtren complies in 2027
options.feedback: Long-lead risks belong on the profile when today's decisions shape them.

options.label: Not yet: three years is outside the planning horizon, and the regulation may change
options.feedback: Then it's too late to change the investment cycle.

options.label: Put it on an emerging-risk watch list and promote it when the regulation is final
options.feedback: Better than nothing, but it needs an owner and actions now.

lesson: An enterprise risk profile aggregates unit risks around strategic objectives, gives each risk an executive owner, and fits on one page.
